messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: GPU pooling alarms in azure-eastus2. Autoscaler failing to provision new vGPU nodes. Queue growth observed for inference-pool (small-models) and large-models. Raising page to oncall.

samantha.le: Ack. Seeing big queue growth on the serving-side. p95 token latency climbed from 450ms -> 2.8s in the last 6m. backlog ~12k requests and enqueue rate is higher than drain rate.

raj.kumar: I can confirm from the cloud console: several allocation attempts returned quota errors. Azure API returned 403/429-ish error: "AllocationFailed: QuotaExceeded - Insufficient regional vGPU quota for subscription" for vm sku Standard_NC6. Autoscaler logs show repeated attempts and backoff.

liam_o: Paste of recent autoscaler snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T02:18:02Z] scaleUp: attempt 7 -> nodeGroup gpu-eastus2
[2026-03-15T02:18:02Z] cloud: allocateMachines -> request 4 x Standard_NC6
[2026-03-15T02:18:03Z] cloud: provider response -> 403 QuotaExceeded
[2026-03-15T02:18:03Z] scaleUp: no capacity found for nodeGroup 'gpu-eastus2' reason=quota
[2026-03-15T02:18:03Z] queue: backlog=12104 drainRate=300/s
```

emily.t: Paging Azure support and opening support ticket now, linking the autoscaler request ids. Also starting a parallel plan: can we divert traffic to eu-west1 as a failover? Cost/latency implications for some customers but better than queueing.

samantha.le: Good. Two quick mitigations in parallel: 1) start regional routing policy change to shift non-SLA traffic and free-tier to eu-west1 / aws-us-west2, 2) throttle background batch ingestion and non-interactive jobs to free up slots. Can someone run a route toggle?

raj.kumar: Routing change queued — preparing canary rule: 10% -> 50% over next 15m for non-paying tenant tag. Putting the rollout into the routing console now. Also adding a model-fallback rule: for non-critical requests use quantized-small if available.

liam_o: Infra-wise, we can also attempt manual spin-up of smaller GPU instances on aws-us-west2 (g4dn.smallish) and register them as a temporary nodeGroup. I'll coordinate with infra-bot to run the bootstrap. Risk: spot eviction on AWS spots.

infra-bot: kickoff: creating temporary nodeGroup gpu-fallback-aws, target=8 nodes, instanceType=g4dn.xlarge. bootstrap script queued: `./bootstrap-node --group gpu-fallback-aws --region us-west-2`

samantha.le: Emily, any ETA from Azure on quota increase? If that's slow we must proceed with cross-region failover. Also prepare a customer-impact blurb for status page.

emily.t: Azure case #152345678 opened. Initial response within 18 mins: case escalated to subscription quota team, estimated review 2-6 hours. Not enough for immediate unblock. I'll post updates. Drafting status update: short notice of degraded performance in eastus2 and active mitigations.

liam_o: Starting manual registration of the aws nodes now. If they come up healthy they should pick up some of the queue. Redirect rule ready to expand if node capacity is observed.

raj.kumar: Quick note: autoscaler has a retry/backoff that currently waits 30s -> 2m between attempts. We should avoid hammering the cloud quota API. Increasing backoff to avoid contributing to API throttling. I'll patch the autoscaler config.

samantha.le: Agreed. Also, implement temporary admission control: set max inflight requests per model per tenant for eastus2 to 2k. That will prevent single noisy tenants from starving the rest.

liam_o: Patch applied to autoscaler backoff and admission control. Monitoring for immediate effects.

infra-bot: aws nodes healthy=3/8 registered, kube labels attached, taints set to gpu-fallback only. kube service discovery show 3 new GPU nodes: gpu-fallback-1..3.

samantha.le: Good. Gradually increase routing weight to aws for non-SLA by 20% increments. Watch end-to-end latency for signed-in enterprise customers and rollback if error rates spike.

raj.kumar: Rolling: 10% -> 30% now. Metrics: backlog reduced from 12.1k -> 8.6k in 9m. p95 down to 1.9s (was 2.8s).

emily.t: Status page draft: "We are investigating capacity issues in the eastus2 region causing delayed responses for some inference requests. We have activated cross-region failover and temporary throttles. Enterprise customers are prioritized; we will update in 30 minutes." Thoughts?

samantha.le: LGTM. Add a note that we are working with our cloud provider and implementing temporary fallbacks. Keep language actionable but not alarmist.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by on-call [samantha.le]. Pager duty handoff scheduled to night-shift at 03:30 UTC with summary below.

samantha.le: Handoff note for night oncall (liam if you're covering): current state - partial mitigation via aws-fallback nodes and routing; azure quota case open; autoscaler backoff increased; backlog reduced but still elevated (~5.2k). Key actions if queue increases: revert routing to heavier failover, throttle background batch jobs, or disable free-tier generation temporarily.

liam_o: I can take the night shift. I'll keep an eye on spot capacity and prepare to spin additional on-demand if spot eviction spikes. If Azure quota comes through we can rebalance back to eastus2.

emily.t: I'll post a 30m update to status and ping customers in the affected list (enterprise contacts) with the mitigation steps and ETA for next update.

samantha.le: Thanks all. Final note: retrospective to capture why we held minimal spare quota in eastus2 and whether we should pre-warm dedicated reservations or implement synthetic draining to keep a small buffer. Adding to ops backlog.

incident-bot: Incident severity remains P1 (degraded) -> monitoring for closure.
